title: Dental-Care Benefits
subtitle: Confirm coverage and price before the chair begins reclining

blocks.text: A dental chair is no place to discover that “covered” and “free” are distant cousins who only exchange holiday cards.

The Canadian Dental Care Plan, or CDCP, helps eligible Canadian residents who lack access to private dental coverage and have adjusted family net income below $90,000. It pays participating oral-health providers according to CDCP rules and established fees. A member may still owe a co-payment, a fee difference or the full cost of an uncovered service.
All four eligibility requirements matter: no access to private dental insurance, required Canadian tax returns filed, adjusted family net income below $90,000 and Canadian residence.

items.title: Confirm the coverage period and provider participation.
Complete a Dental Coverage and Cost Confirmation Sheet.
“Declining available workplace dental insurance makes me eligible for CDCP.”
items.text: Access to private coverage can make a person ineligible even when they choose not to enrol or pay the premium. The plan checks access, not enthusiasm.

sections.title: Coverage Has Dates, Percentages and Rules

blocks.text: After approval, the member receives a coverage start date and information from Service Canada and Sun Life. Do not book treatment before coverage begins. CDCP does not reimburse members who pay the full bill themselves; the provider submits eligible claims directly.

items.title: AFNI BELOW $70,000
items.text: CDCP covers 100% of eligible services at CDCP established fees; additional provider charges can still remain.

items.title: AFNI $70,000 TO $79,999
items.text: CDCP covers 60% of established fees and the member co-payment is 40%, plus possible additional charges.

items.title: AFNI $80,000 TO $89,999
items.text: CDCP covers 40% of established fees and the member co-payment is 60%, plus possible additional charges.

items.title: AFNI $90,000 OR MORE
items.text: The income requirement is not met for that benefit period.

blocks.text: A provider’s usual fee may be higher than the CDCP established fee. Ask whether the office will charge the difference—often called balance billing—before treatment.
CDCP can coordinate with certain provincial, territorial and federal dental programs. Coordination rules vary, so show every coverage letter to the provider.

items.title: “A 0% co-payment means the appointment must cost the member nothing.”
items.text: Zero per cent applies to eligible CDCP services at established fees. Uncovered services and provider fees above the CDCP amount can still create a bill.

sections.title: Ask Four Questions Before Saying Yes

blocks.text: Estimate before the chair reclines, not after.
Preauthorization is a coverage review, not permission for treatment and not a promise that every future charge will be paid. The provider submits it with supporting documents.
Frequency limits matter. A service can appear in the benefits guide and still be unavailable because the allowed interval or quantity has already been used.

items.title: “If a dentist recommends a service, CDCP must cover it.”
items.text: Clinical recommendation and benefit coverage answer different questions. The provider decides care with the patient; the plan applies coverage criteria.

blocks.text: Key takeaway: CDCP membership is not a blank cheque. Confirm the coverage date, service code, preauthorization, established fee, co-payment and provider difference before treatment begins.

sections.title: Renée and the Crown With Two Prices

paragraphs: Renée Gagnon in Moncton had CDCP coverage and needed a crown. The clinic said the service was “covered,” a word Renée’s budget interpreted as “please leave your wallet in the car.”
The conflict appeared in the estimate. The crown required preauthorization, Renée had a 40% co-payment and the clinic’s fee exceeded the CDCP established amount. Covered did not mean fully paid.

The provider submitted the request, then gave Renée a written breakdown: plan payment, co-payment, fee difference and an alternative treatment discussion. Renée waited for the coverage decision before choosing with her dentist.
The crown did not become inexpensive by vocabulary. It became understandable, which is the useful first step between a treatment plan and a payment plan.

blocks.text: Never rely on a verbal percentage alone. Ask for the procedure codes and member estimate so the provider and patient are discussing the same service, tooth and fee.
Covered is a coverage category, not a price. Confirm the codes, preauthorization and fee breakdown in writing before agreeing to treatment.

sections.title: Quick Check: Choose the Best Next Move

items.title: What four requirements form the CDCP eligibility screen?
items.detail: No access to private dental insurance, required Canadian tax returns filed, adjusted family net income below $90,000 and Canadian residence.

items.title: Why can a member with a 0% co-payment still owe money?
items.detail: Zero per cent applies to eligible CDCP services at established fees; uncovered services and provider fees above the CDCP amount can still create a bill.

items.title: Who submits an eligible CDCP claim?
items.detail: The participating provider submits eligible claims directly; CDCP does not reimburse members who pay the full bill themselves.

items.title: What does preauthorization decide—and not decide?
items.detail: It is a coverage review completed before specified treatment; it is not permission for treatment and not a promise that every future charge will be paid.

items.title: Why should all provincial or federal dental coverage be disclosed?
items.detail: CDCP can coordinate with certain provincial, territorial and federal dental programs, and coordination rules vary, so every coverage letter should reach the provider.

sections.title: Your Action: Complete Your Dental Coverage and Cost Confirmation Sheet

blocks.text: Do not record member identifiers, health numbers or full clinical records. Keep the official letters and estimates securely.
CDCP coverage must be renewed annually. Missing the renewal window can create a coverage gap, and services received during the gap are not reimbursed later.

items.title: Established fee
items.text: Amount CDCP uses to calculate payment.

items.title: Co-payment
items.text: Member percentage of the CDCP established fee.

items.title: Balance billing
items.text: Provider charge above the plan's established fee.

items.title: Preauthorization
items.text: Coverage review completed before specified treatment.

items.title: Frequency limit
items.text: Maximum number or interval for covered services.
